newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, then slips after AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, then slips after AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, hit by technical selling when upside momentum stalled early, ended broadly lower Wednesday in active trade, then slipped more on ACCESS after a bearish weekly inventory report.

July tumbled 5.9 cents to close at $2.227 per million British thermal units, then slipped to $2.21 in after-hours ACCESS trade. August settled 5.6 cents lower at $2.213. Other deferreds ended down by 1.2 to 4.3 cents.
"It was a huge number, but with the heat, there's still some short covering holding it up," said one Midwest trader.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 97 bcf, well above average estimates in the 85-90 bcf range. Overall stocks climbed to 233 bcf, or 19 percent, above year-ago levels. Eastern inventories increased by 65 bcf and remained 100 bcf, or 15 percent, over last year. Consuming region west storage, which gained 10 bcf last week, continued to lag 1996 levels by about 10 percent. Stocks in the producing region held at 54 percent above last year.
With some unplanned East Coast nuclear plant outages this week and more Midwest and Northeast heat forecast, few expected prices to crater near-term.
But many agreed the market was due for a pullback after six straight up days, adding comfortable stocks, particularly after this week's jump, left operators with more discretion.

In the East, unplanned outages were reported this week at PECO's 1,055 MW Limerick 1, GPU's 786 MW Three Mile Island 1 and Duke's 846 MW Oconee 3. All were expected to remain off line until early next week.
Chart traders pegged July support at the $2.151 double bottom, then at $2.13, $2.055 and $2. Resistance was seen at $2.305 and then at $2.37 and the contract high of $2.44.

But with July set to go off the board Thursday, traders turned their attention to August, where trendline resistance was seen at $2.28 and further selling likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high. Support was pegged at $2.145 and then at the recent $2.08 low.

In the cash Tuesday, Louisiana Gulf Coast prices were talked little changed in the high-$2.20s. Midcon pipes also held steady in the low-teens. New York city gate gas also finished unchanged in the low-$2.60s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip skidded 3.1 cents to $2.271. NYMEX said 64,218 contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 55,266.

On the KCBT, July expired 1.6 cents lower at $2.133, while deferreds ended down by 2.5 to 4.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 4.3 cents to 9.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 1,255 lots traded, up sharply from Tuesday's total of 542.
